newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: New Malaysian fund not a departure from policies.
newsitem.headline: New Malaysian fund not a departure from policies.

text.p: Malaysia's first government-managed unit trust fund open to all ethnic groups is not a departure from national economic policy which promotes ethnic Malays, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Wednesday.

In launching the three billion ringgit ($1.20 billion) Amanah Saham Wawasan 2020, or ASW 2020, Mahathir said that the country was not ready to abandon its New Economic Policy (NEP) begun after racial riots in 1969.

"There still exists disparity between the communities which reflects the imbalance in the situation. So we have not achieved the new economic policy," Mahathir told a group of about 2,500 schoolchildren, who are among those targeted by the new fund.

The NEP sought to redistribute wealth in the Chinese-dominated economy in favour of Bumiputeras, or ethnic Malays, some 25 years ago. Mahathir said that while adjustments can be made in line with the country's rapid economic development, the NEP is still essential.

Previous government-managed unit trusts were restricted to Bumiputeras, but the ASW 2020 targets all Malaysians aged between 12 and 29, who make up about 40 percent of Malaysia's 20 million population.
In the breakdown, 51 percent of the fund will be set aside for Bumiputeras and the rest for non-Bumiputeras, who consist of Chinese, Indians and other ethnic groups.
It will invest in stocks and money market instruments and eventually in overseas markets.

The fund aims to promote savings by younger Malaysians and provide financing for infrastructure and privatised projects. At the launching ceremony on Wednesday, the audience was shown a video of the advertisement for the fund in three languages.

ASW 2020 carries not only Malaysia's hopes for elevating its nascent fund management industry but takes its very name from the political and social "Vision 2020" of evolving into an industrialised nation by that year.
By that time, Malaysia reckons some of ASW 2020's investors will be approaching retirement age, and the unit trust is also being marketed as a pension scheme.
Malaysia wants to increase its savings rate to 40 percent of gross domestic product by 2000, from the current 34.60 percent.

The minimum investment for an individual is 100 ringgit and 5,000 ringgit for an institution. The maximum investment is 50,000 ringgit for an individual with the institution cap at the fund managers' discretion.
